title: security.txt should declare the URI it is served from as Canonical

spec.name: RFC 9116
spec.normative_quote: The "Canonical" field indicates the canonical URIs where the "security.txt" file is located, which is usually something like "https://example.com/.well-known/security.txt".
spec.note: Transcribed from a live fetch of https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9116.txt on 2026-08-31. conformance_testable is false on purpose: §2.5 states 'Unless otherwise stated, all fields MUST be considered optional', and §2.5.2 states no exception, so RFC 9116 imposes NO obligation to publish a Canonical field. The quote is descriptive, and the obligation this rule enforces is local -- see policy_note.

policy_note: RFC 9116 does not require Canonical. This repo publishes one anyway, and this rule guards that choice, because §2.5.2 ties consumer trust to the retrieval URI appearing among the canonical fields (see security-txt-canonical-mismatch): with no Canonical field at all, a researcher can never make that determination for our file. Severity is warn, not fail -- an absent optional field is a regression against our own policy, not a broken artifact, so it must be visible without failing the audit (lib/http.mjs reports warns and exits 0). Fail is reserved for the mismatch case, where a Canonical field is present and actively points elsewhere.
applicability: A security.txt body of any length.
expectation: The body contains at least one line matching /^Canonical:[ \t]*\S/ (case-insensitive, per-line).

cases.name: Canonical present and correct -- this rule does not fire
Canonical present but pointing elsewhere -- this rule does not fire, security-txt-canonical-mismatch does
